Joint and tensor factorization: EB-CP and block EBMF

coordination_joint.Rmd

The default cellprograms pipeline fits each cell type separately and only then asks whether programs are shared. Two experimental (v0.2.0.9001) extensions invert the ordering and factorize across cell types directly:

  • EB-CP (fit_eb_cp() / eb_cp_from_fit()): a tensor-style greedy EBMF over the stacked cell-type x donor matrices. Each rank-1 component is a gene loading (U), a donor activity vector (V) shared across the cell types the component spans, and a cell-type loading vector (W). Components are accepted by a held-out z gate on a donor-synchronous split, so the number of components is selected by out-of-sample predictive evidence, not by a variance cutoff.
  • Block EBMF (fit_joint_block() / block_clusters()): a shared-first flashier pass over the stacked expression matrix, followed by per-cell-type private passes on the residuals. block_clusters() collapses shared factors into gene-set clusters by loading overlap and returns donor activity per cluster.

This vignette runs both on a small simulated dataset and states the scope caveats measured in the coordination benchmark (see benchmarks/coordination/ in the repository).

library(cellprograms)

sim <- simulate_pseudobulk(scenario = "mixed", n_samples = 60,
                           n_genes = 800, program_size = 40, seed = 1)
x <- as_cell_program_data(sim$pseudobulk)
fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                             max_factors = 10L, seed = 1)
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)

EB-CP: greedy components with held-out selection

eb_cp_from_fit() runs EB-CP on the adjusted per-cell-type matrices of a fitted cell_program_fit. If strata is not supplied, the donor-synchronous train/held-out split is derived from the covariates used at fit time, so the split respects the adjustment; pass strata explicitly when you want a different stratification.

cp <- eb_cp_from_fit(fit)
cp$n_components
#> [1] 8
cp$kept_heldout_z          # held-out z of each kept component
#> [1] 141.06089 154.97144 103.76617 107.39676  94.15278  63.45945  93.65694
#> [8]  51.93119
cp$trace_z                 # z trace including the first failed component
#> [1] 141.06089 154.97144 103.76617 107.39676  94.15278  63.45945  93.65694
#> [8]  51.93119

eb_cp_programs() turns components into program calls. Components spanning >= min_members cell types at the membership threshold are flagged as coordination programs; the rest are kept as private programs, flagged rather than dropped.

pr <- eb_cp_programs(cp)
pr$programs
#>   program cell_type n_members is_coordination heldout_z
#> 1    CP01      Mono         1           FALSE 141.06089
#> 2    CP02    CD8+NK         2            TRUE 154.97144
#> 3    CP03         B         1           FALSE 103.76617
#> 4    CP04       CD4         1           FALSE 107.39676
#> 5    CP05        NK         1           FALSE  94.15278
#> 6    CP06      Mono         1           FALSE  63.45945
#> 7    CP07    CD8+NK         2            TRUE  93.65694
#> 8    CP08         B         1           FALSE  51.93119
head(pr$activity[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])   # donor activity per coordination component
#>        cluster_02  cluster_07
#> obs1   2.53382698 -2.76698019
#> obs10  0.49417548 -0.54670036
#> obs11 -0.36878957  0.34052851
#> obs12 -1.12515663  1.19204711
#> obs13 -0.07259629  0.05518669
#> obs14 -0.71861307  0.58362302

Block EBMF: shared-first pass plus private residuals

fit_joint_block() stacks the per-cell-type matrices and fits shared factors first, then per-cell-type private factors on the residuals.

bfit <- fit_joint_block(fit, level = "expression", order = "shared_first",
                        max_factors = 10L, seed = 1, verbose = 0L)
bfit$shared_fit$n_factors
#> [1] 4
bc <- block_clusters(bfit, mass_thresh = 0.1)
head(bc$clusters, 10)
#>   cluster cell_type program_id      stat fwer_p
#> 1       1         B       SF01 0.3283760     NA
#> 2       1       CD4       SF01 0.3283760     NA
#> 3       1        NK       SF01 0.3283760     NA
#> 4       1      Mono       SF01 0.3283760     NA
#> 5       2       CD8       SF02 0.5278789     NA
#> 6       2        NK       SF02 0.5278789     NA

Each row of bc$clusters is a gene-set cluster (a group of shared factors with overlapping loadings); bc$activity holds donor activity per cluster. The block-mass rule (mass_thresh) keeps clusters whose membership spreads across at least two cell types.

Scope caveats from the coordination benchmark

Both extensions trade robustness for directness, and the preregistered coordination benchmark (benchmarks/coordination/, tag prereg-coord-v1) quantifies where:

  • Block EBMF (block_E) is powerful but over-calls without calibration. On null data the shared-first pass still returns factors whose loadings spread across blocks, and the block-mass rule alone called spurious shared programs in 16/16 null replicates. A permutation-calibrated significance layer (within-strata donor permutation, max-T family-wise control) is available in the benchmark harness and is being productized; until then, treat uncalibrated block_clusters() output as a candidate list, not as evidence of sharing.
  • EB-CP is conservative. The held-out z gate keeps specificity high (near-zero false positives on null data) but loses power when shared programs have cell-type-specific gene loadings, because the model’s shared donor-activity assumption is only approximately met.
  • Low-K regime. Both methods were validated with few recurring programs (1-3) against many private ones. With dozens of true per-cell-type programs, set max_factors above the default and expect the shared-first ordering to matter more.

For the default-by-construction path (per-cell-type fits, then sharing_spectrum() / plot_sharing_spectrum()), see vignette("quickstart").
